messages.author: 23e9c489ea8b313a
messages.subject: cholesky_factor_corr and standard deviations to cholesky_factor_cov?
parts:
I am back trying to adjust myself to Stan syntax.  As I understand the approach to incorporating the covariance matrix, say as the covariance of vector-valued random effects in a mixed-effects model, the distribution is defined on the correlation matrix but it is the choleksy factor of the covariance matrix that is used in multi_normal_cholesky.

I seem to be confused about what a cholesky_factor_corr is and whether it can be used as a matrix in a multiplication or in multi_normal_cholesky.

Suppose I have a very simple case like

parameters {
  cholesky_factor_corr[J] L;    // Cholesky factor of unconditional correlation of random effects
#  vector[J]  tau;                // Unconditional standard deviations of the random effects
  vector[J] b[N]; // random effects on original scale
  vector[K] beta; // fixed-effects
  real<lower=0> sigma; // standard deviation of response given random effects
}

model {
#  tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  L ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  for (j in 1:J)
    b[j] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(0,L);
  for (n in 1:N)
    y[n] ~ normal(dot(Xt[n],beta) + dot(Zt[n],b[subj[n]]),sigma);
}

This fails to compile, apparently because L is not a matrix.

Do I need to do something to make L act like a matrix?  

Once I get past this I want to incorporate tau in the model.

messages.author: 89abf8a3796a510b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr and standard deviations to cholesky_factor_cov?
parts:
That error message is saying that multi_normal_log can't be called with the signature vector, integer, matrix. It's because you're using:

b[j] ~ multi_normal_log(0, L) 

When you should be using:

 b[j] ~ multi_normal_log(rep_vector(0, J), L) 

multi_normal_log needs the dimensionally of the first two arguments to match (as well as the type). 

cholesky_factor_corr can indeed be used in multiplications, but if you want to use it for multi_normal_log, you'll need to use code in the transformed parameters block to turn it into a proper covariance matrix by multiplying by a vector of standard deviations 2X. 

Rob

messages.author: 89abf8a3796a510b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr and standard deviations to cholesky_factor_cov?
parts:
Apologies on that last piece of advice, it was wrong. Just add the block:

transformed parameters {
cholesky_factor_cov[J] chol_mat;

chol_mat <- diag_pre_multily(tau, L)
}

And change your tau line to read:

vector<lower=0> tau;

And your multi_normal_log line to:

b[j] ~ multi_normal_log(rep_vector(0,J), chol_mat)

The best advice for putting a multivariate normal prior on your beta's will be on page 63 of the manual. Following that code will allow you to do away with your multi_normal_log statement. 

Rob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr and standard deviations to cholesky_factor_cov?
parts:
> On Mar 18, 2015, at 8:10 AM, Robert Trangucci <robert.t...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Apologies on that last piece of advice, it was wrong. Just add the block:
>
> transformed parameters {
> cholesky_factor_cov[J] chol_mat;
>
> chol_mat <- diag_pre_multily(tau, L)
> }
>

I would strongly suggest using cholesky_factor_corr here
and an LKJ prior which is like the beta but for correlation
matrices --- as the dof parameter goes up, it concentrates
mass around the unit matrix.

It's just a more interpretable way of doing what Andrew and
Jennifer were suggesting in their regression book.

Ben has a very nice paper on the LKJ vs. Wisharts:

http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/unpublished/Visualization.pdf

> And change your tau line to read:
>
> vector<lower=0> tau;
>
> And your multi_normal_log line to:
>
> b[j] ~ multi_normal_log(rep_vector(0,J), chol_mat)

I'd also suggest defining rep_vector(0,J) in the transformed
data block so it's only allocated and filled once.

Then doesn't this have to be multi_normal_cholesky(...).
What you have won't work, as it needs to be multi_normal(), not
multi_normal_log --- the former is the sampling statement syntax,
the latter the function name.
> The best advice for putting a multivariate normal prior on your beta's will be on page 63 of the manual. Following that code will allow you to do away with your multi_normal_log statement.
